title: ENFORCEMENT DECREE OF THE LIFELONG EDUCATION ACT
full_text:
CHAPTER I GENERAL PROVISIONS

Article 1 (Purpose) The purpose of this Decree is to prescribe matters delegated by the Lifelong Education Act and other matters necessary for the enforcement thereof.

Article 2 (Use of public facilities) When any person who conducts lifelong education utilizes public facilities under Article 7 of the Lifelong Education Act (hereinafter referred to as the "Act"), he or she may ask a manager of such public facilities for assistance from the employees in charge of managing the relevant public facilities and cooperation from them in the use of necessary equipment.

CHAPTER II MASTER PLANS FOR LIFELONG EDUCATION PROMOTION

Article 3 (Formulation and Implementation of Master Plans) (1) The Minister of Education shall listen to the opinions of the head of the central administrative agency related to the business of lifelong education at the time of establishing a master plan for lifelong education promotion under Article 9 of the Act. <Amended on Feb. 29, 2008; Mar. 23, 2013>
  (2) The Minister of Education shall confirm a draft of the master plan for lifelong education promotion, subject to the deliberation of the Lifelong Education Promotion Committee under Article 10 of the Act (hereinafter referred to as the "Promotion Committee"). <Amended on Feb. 29, 2008; Mar. 23, 2013>
  (3) Deleted. <Apr. 16, 2024>
  [Title Amended on Apr. 16, 2024]

Article 3-2 (Formulation and Implementation of Annual Implementation Plans) (1) The Minister of Education shall prepare guidelines necessary for the formulation of an annual implementation plan for lifelong education promotion (hereinafter referred to as "implementation plan") by the head of a relevant central administrative agency and the Special Metropolitan City Mayor, a Metropolitan City Mayor, a Special Self-Governing City Mayor, a Do Governor, or a Special Self-Governing Province Governor (hereinafter referred to as "Mayor/Do Governor") pursuant to Article 11 of the Act, and notify the head of the relevant central administrative agency and the relevant Mayor/Do Governor of such guidelines by Dec. 31 of the year preceding the year in which the implementation plan is implemented.
  (2) The heads of relevant central administrative agencies and Mayors/Do Governors shall submit the following matters to the Minister of Education by the end of February every year pursuant to Article 11 (2) of the Act:
  1. Results of implementation of implementation plans for the previous year;
  2. Implementation plan for the relevant year.
  (3) The Minister of Education shall integrate the implementation plans submitted pursuant to paragraph (2) and notify the heads of relevant central administrative agencies and Mayors/Do Governors thereof.
  (4) The Minister of Education shall evaluate the performance results of the implementation plans for the previous year submitted pursuant to paragraph (2) 1 after deliberation by the Promotion Committee, and notify the heads of relevant central administrative agencies and Mayors/Do Governors of the results thereof each year.
  (5) The heads of relevant central administrative agencies and Mayors/Do Governors shall reflect the results of evaluation notified by the Minister of Education pursuant to paragraph (4) in the implementation plan for the following year.
  [This Article Added on Apr. 16, 2024]

Article 4 (Matters to be deliberated by promotion committee) "Matters prescribed by Presidential Decree" in Article 10 (2) 5 of the Act means any of the following: <Amended on Apr.16, 2024>
  1. Matters concerning expansion of foundations of lifelong education, such as facilities and equipment for lifelong education;
  2. Matters concerning improvement of system, such as operation of study record systems and promotion of utilizing study results;
  3. Matters concerning the creation and support for lifelong study culture;
  4. Other matters which the chairperson of the Promotion Committee deems necessary and requests the deliberation of the Promotion Committee.

Article 5 (Organization and operation of promotion committee) (1) In accordance with Article 10 (4) of the Act, the Minister of Education shall commission the following persons as members of the Promotion Committee. In such cases, up to ten members shall be commissioned from among those falling under subparagraph 2: <Amended on Feb. 20, 2018>
  1. The Vice Minister of Economy and Finance, the Vice Minister of the Interior and Safety, the Vice Minister of Culture, Sports and Tourism, the Vice Minister of Agriculture, Food and Rural Affairs, the Vice Minister of Trade, Industry and Energy, the Vice Minister of Health and Welfare, the Vice Minister of Employment and Labor, the Vice Minister of Gender Equality and Family, and the Vice Minister of SMEs and Startups. In such cases, where there are multiple Vice Ministers in a certain Ministry, the Vice Minister designated by the Minister of the relevant Ministry shall serve as a member;
  2. Persons who have sufficient knowledge and experience in lifelong education, such as experts in the fields of lifelong education and education for persons with disabilities.
  (2) The term of office of the members of the Promotion Committee shall be according to the following classifications, and any member falling under paragraph (1) 2 may be consecutively reappointed: <Amended on Feb. 20, 2018>
  1. Members falling under paragraph (1) 1: While they are serving as a Vice Minister;
  2. Members falling under paragraph (1) 2: Two years.
  (3) The chairperson shall exercise overall control of the affairs of the Promotion Committee and represent it.
  (4) Where the chairperson is unable to perform his or her duties due to any unavoidable reasons, the member who is designated in advance by the chairperson may act as a chairperson on his or her behalf.
  (5) The meetings of the Promotion Committee shall be convened by the chairperson, constituted by the attendance of a majority of all incumbent members and resolutions shall be made by the consent of a majority of those present.
  (6) Where the chairperson intends to convene a meeting of the National Institute for Lifelong Education, he or she shall give a written notice on the date, time, venue, and agenda of the meeting to each member seven days prior to the opening of the meeting; provided, this shall not apply where the meeting is convened urgently or where any unavoidable reason exists to the contrary.
  (7) If deemed necessary, the chairperson may have any public official of the relevant central administrative agency attend the Promotion Committee and state his or her opinions with regard to his or her duties.
  (8) The Promotion Committee shall have a practical mediation committee for lifelong education to efficiently support the deliberation of the Promotion Committee and its organization and operation shall be prescribed by Decree of the Ministry of Education. <Amended on Feb. 29, 2008; Mar. 23, 2013>

Article 5-2 (Removal of commissioned members) The Minister of Education may remove a member of the Promotion Committee if the member falls under any of the following:
  1. If he or she becomes unable to perform his or her duties due to mental disorder;
  2. If he or she has committed any misconduct in connection with his or her duties;
  3. If he or she is deemed inappropriate as a committee member due to negligence of duties or injury to dignity, or for any other reason;
  4. If he or she voluntarily informs that circumstances prevent him or her from performing his or her duties.
  [This Article Added on Dec. 31, 2015]

Article 6 (Secretary of the promotion committee and allowance) (1) The Promotion Committee shall have one secretary to deal with its duties, who shall be appointed by the chairperson from among the public officials belonging to the Ministry of Education. <Amended on Feb. 29, 2008; Mar. 23, 2013>
  (2) Any allowances and travel expenses may be paid and reimbursed to the members present at the Promotion Committee within the budget; provided, this shall not apply where the members who are the public officials attend the Promotion Committee directly related to their duties.

Article 7 (National lifelong study city council) (1) A national lifelong study city council under Article 15 (2) of the Act (hereinafter referred to as the "national lifelong study city council") shall be comprised of the head of a Special Self-Governing City designated by the Minister of Education as a lifelong study city, the head of a Si (including an administrative city under Article 10 (2) of the Special Act on the Establishment of Jeju Special Self-Governing Province and the Development of Free International City), Gun, and autonomous Gu and the heads of the district offices of education. <Amended on Feb. 29, 2008; Mar. 23, 2013; Dec. 9, 2021>
  (2) The State and local governments may subsidize human resources and expenses necessary for the operation and activity of the City Council.

Article 7-2 (National council on lifelong study cities for persons with disabilities) Article 7 shall apply mutatis mutandis to the composition and operation of the National Council for Lifelong Learning Cities for Persons with Disabilities under Article 15-2 (2) of the Act. In such cases, "City Council" shall be construed as "National Council for Lifelong Learning Cities for Persons with Disabilities"; and "lifelong learning cities" as "lifelong learning cities for persons with disabilities."
  [This Article Added on Dec. 9, 2021]x
  [Previous Article 7-2 moved to Article 7-4 <Dec. 9, 2021>]

Article 7-3 (Consultative body for revitalizing lifelong study cities for persons with disabilities) (1) The consultative body for revitalizing lifelong study cities for persons with disabilities under Article 15-2 (5) of the Act (hereinafter referred to as "consultative body for lifelong study cities for persons with disabilities") shall be established under the jurisdiction of the Minister of Education.
  (2) The chairperson of the consultative body for lifelong study cities for persons with disabilities shall be the Minister of Education and members thereof shall be the following persons:
  1. The Minister of Health and Welfare and the Minister of Employment and Labor;
  2. The head of institutions related to lifelong study cities for persons with disabilities, such as the Korea Disabled People’s Development Institute under Article 29-2 of the Act on Welfare of Persons with Disabilities, the Korea Employment Agency for Persons with Disabilities under Article 43 of the Act on the Employment Promotion and Vocational Rehabilitation of Persons with Disabilities, and the National Lifelong Education Promotion Center for Persons with Disabilities under Article 19-2 of the Act;
  (3) The Minister of Education may subsidize expenses incurred in operating the consultative body for lifelong study cities for persons with disabilities and conducting its activities.
  (4) Except as provided in paragraphs (1) through (3), details necessary for organizing and operating the consultative body for lifelong study cities for persons with disabilities shall be determined by the Minister of Education.
  [This Article Added on Dec. 9, 2021]x

Article 7-4 (Issuance of lifelong education vouchers) (1) A person who intends to be issued a lifelong education voucher pursuant to Article 16-2 (1) of the Act shall file an application therefor with the Minister of Education or the head of a local government, as prescribed by Decree of the Ministry of Education. <Amended on Dec. 9, 2021>
  (2) Persons having priorities in applying for the issuance of lifelong education vouchers under Article 16-2 (2) of the Act shall be as follows: <Amended on Dec. 9, 2021; Sep. 26, 2023>
  1. Recipients and the second-lowest income bracket provided in the National Basic Living Security Act;
  2. Persons who receive disability allowances prescribed in Article 49 of the Act on Welfare of Persons with Disabilities;
  3. Recipients under the Disability Pension Act;
  4. Persons eligible for support under Articles 5 and 5-2 of the Single-Parent Family Support Act;
  5. Persons whose economic status, such as household income or property, meet the criteria determined and publicly notified by the Minister of Education.
  (3) "Data prescribed by Presidential Decree, such as a family relation certificate and data on national tax and local tax" in the former part of Article 16-2 (3) of the Act means the data specified in Appendix 1. <Amended on Dec. 9, 2021>
  (4) The Minister of Education and the heads of local governments may build and operate an information system to efficiently conduct duties related to lifelong education vouchers, including the issuance, management of use, etc. of lifelong education vouchers. <Amended on Dec. 9, 2021>
  (5) Except as provided in paragraphs (1) through (4), matters necessary for the application, issuance, management of use, etc. of lifelong education vouchers shall be determined by the Minister of Education. <Amended on Dec. 9, 2021>
  [This Article Added on Feb. 20, 2018]
  [Title Amended on Dec. 9, 2021]
  [Moved from Article 7-2 <Dec. 9, 2021>]

Article 7-5 (Designation of institution dedicated to affairs regarding lifelong education vouchers) (1) The head of a local government may designate a dedicated institution under Article 16-2 (5) of the Act (hereinafter referred to as "institution dedicated to lifelong education vouchers"), from among the following institutions or corporations:
  1. The City/Do institute for lifelong education under Article 20 of the Act;
  2. Other institutions or corporations prescribed by ordinance of the relevant local government, which are institutions or corporations with expertise in the performance of duties related to lifelong education.
  (2) The institution dedicated to lifelong education vouchers shall perform the following affairs:
  1. The issuance and management of use of lifelong education vouchers;
  2. Consultation on the use of lifelong education vouchers;
  3. The establishment and operation of an information system to conduct the affairs provided in subparagraphs 1 and 2;
  4. Other affairs the head of a local government deems necessary to efficiently conduct the affairs regarding lifelong education vouchers.
  (3) The head of a local government may provide support to cover expenses incurred by an institution dedicated to lifelong education vouchers in performing its affairs.
  [This Article Added on Dec. 9, 2021]x

Article 7-6 (Use of lifelong education vouchers) (1) A person who intends to use a lifelong education voucher pursuant to Article 16-3 (1) of the Act shall produce an identification card issued by a public institution, such as a resident registration certificate (including mobile certificate), with which his or her identity can be verified, to a person who provides a lifelong education program. <Amended on Dec. 3, 2024>
  (2) When the Minister of Education or the head of a local government intends to withdraw a lifelong education voucher or recover all or some of an amount equivalent to the amount stated on the lifelong education voucher pursuant to Article 16-3 (4) of the Act, he or she shall give written notice to the person who has been issued a lifelong education voucher of the following matters:
  1. In cases of withdrawal: Reasons for withdrawal, deadline for withdrawal, methods of withdrawal, etc.;
  2. In cases of recovery: Grounds for recovery, amount to be recovered, payment deadline, payment institution, payment method, etc.
  [This Article Added on Dec. 9, 2021]x

Article 7-7 (Designation of national lifelong education statistics center) The Minister of Education may designate a national lifelong education statistics center pursuant to Article 18 (5) of the Act from among the following institutions or corporations to perform duties such as the statistical survey on lifelong education:
  1. The Korean Educational Development Institute under Article 8 of the Act on the Establishment, Operation and Fostering of Government-Funded Research Institutes;
  2. Other institutions or corporations that have expertise in conducting duties related to the statistical survey, etc. of lifelong education.
  [This Article Added on Dec. 9, 2021]x

Article 7-8 (Establishment and operation of comprehensive information system for lifelong education) (1) The scope and contents of information to be contained in the comprehensive information system for lifelong education referred to in Article 18-2 (1) of the Act shall be as follows. In such cases, where any personal information is included in the information to be contained, the prior consent of the data subject under the Personal Information Protection Act shall be obtained:
  1. Status of lifelong education programs;
  2. Status of institutions operating lifelong education programs;
  3. Various statistics and the results of fact-finding surveys related to lifelong education programs;
  4. Status of lecturers in lifelong education programs;
  5. Status of learners in lifelong education programs;
  6. Information contained in the study record system under Article 14 (5);
  7. Other information determined by the Minister of education in relation to lifelong education.
  (2) The Minister of Education shall manage information under paragraph (1) in accordance with the following standards:
  1. Ensuring security to prevent information from being lost, stolen, leaked, forged, altered, or damaged;
  2. Information shall be kept up-to-date, accurate, and interlinked.
  [This Article Added on Dec. 9, 2021]x

CHAPTER III NATIONAL INSTITUTE FOR LIFELONG EDUCATION

Article 8 (Request for and payment of contributions) (1) Where the National Institute for Lifelong Education under Article 19 (1) of the Act (hereinafter referred to as "National Institute for Lifelong Education") intends to receive a contribution from the State under Article 19 (7) of the Act, it shall submit the following documents to the Minister of Education not later than April 30 every year: <Amended on Feb. 29, 2008; Mar. 23, 2013; Dec. 9, 2021>
  1. Request for contribution per project cost, operating expense and facility cost for the following year;
  2. Business plan for the following year;
  3. Data that can explain the contents of the request for contribution.
  (2) Once a contribution is finalized, the Minister of Education shall give notice to the National Institute for Lifelong Education thereof. <Amended on Feb. 29, 2008; Mar. 23, 2013>
  (3) Where the National Institute for Lifelong Education intends to receive a contribution under paragraph (2), it shall attach a quarterly business plan and a budget execution plan to an application for contribution and file them with the Minister of Education. <Amended on Feb. 29, 2008; Mar. 23, 2013>

Article 9 (Management of contributions) The National Institute for Lifelong Education shall, upon receiving a contribution, establish a separate account for each project cost, operating expense and facility cost and manage them.

Article 10 (Filing of settlement of accounts) The National Institute for Lifelong Education shall file the business results of every fiscal year and settlement of accounts audited by a certified public accountant or accounting corporation with the Minister of Education not later than March 31 of the following year. <Amended on Feb. 29, 2008; Mar. 23, 2013>

Article 11 (Treatment of surplus) The National Institute for Lifelong Education shall, if any surplus accrues in settlement of accounts in any fiscal year, use such surplus to offset any loss brought forward and include the remainder, if any, in a revenue for the following year or accumulate it as reserve of basic property under the articles of association.

Article 11-2 (National lifelong education promotion center for persons with disabilities) (1) The National Lifelong Education Promotion Center for Persons with Disabilities referred to in Article 19-2 (1) of the Act (hereinafter referred to as "National Lifelong Education Promotion Center for Persons with Disabilities") shall be established by the Minister of Education.
  (2) The National Lifelong Education Promotion Center for Persons with Disabilities may, when it is necessary to conduct its duties, request cooperation from related institutions and organizations, such as central administrative agencies and local governments.
  [This Article Added on May 29, 2017]

Article 11-3 (Human rights education for persons who engage in lifelong education for persons with disabilities) (1) Education on the human rights of persons with disabilities for persons who engage in lifelong education for persons with disabilities under Article 19-3 (1) of the Act (hereafter in this Article referred to as "education on the human rights of persons with disabilities") shall include the following matters:
  1. Matters regarding the protection of the human rights and the rights and interests of persons with disabilities;
  2. Matters regarding statutes, regulations, and systems related to the human rights of persons with disabilities;
  3. Matters regarding cases on discrimination between persons with disabilities and persons without disabilities;
  4. Matters regarding domestic and foreign information trends in the protection of the human rights of persons with disabilities;
  5. Other matters that the Minister of Education deems necessary to protect the human rights of persons with disabilities.
  (2) Education on the human rights of persons with disabilities shall be conducted collectively and may, if necessary, be provided by means of distance education using Internet lectures, etc.
  [This Article Added on Oct. 22, 2019]

Article 12 (Operation of city/do institute for lifelong education) (1) If the Mayor/Do Governor intends to establish or designate a City/Do institute for lifelong education under Article 20 (1) of the Act (hereinafter referred to as "City/Do institute"), he or she shall consult with the City/Do superintendent of education.
  (2) The City/Do institute shall be equipped with necessary organization and facilities for the performance of duties referred to in Article 20 (2) of the Act and necessary matters concerning the organization, facilities and procedures for designation, etc. required for its operation shall be determined by ordinance of the relevant local government.
  (3) The National Council of City/Do Institute for Lifelong Education and Promotion under Article 20 (3) of the Act shall be comprised of the heads of City/Do Institutes. <Added on on Apr. Apr. 16, 2024>
  (4) A Local Government may subsidize expenses necessary for the operation and activities of the National Council of City/Do Institutes for Lifelong Education and Promotion, within budgetary limits. <Added on on Apr. Apr. 16, 2024>

Article 12-2 (Operation of programs of lifelong education facilities for persons with disabilities) Where the State, a local government, or a City/Do superintendent of education operates a lifelong educational program customized for each type of disability pursuant to the latter part of Article 20-2 (1) of the Act, he or she shall provide necessary convenience, such as Korean sign language, closed subtitles, braille subtitles, assistants, and assistive personnel and assistive devices, in consideration of the type, condition, etc. of disability of persons with disabilities.
  [This Article Added on Apr. 16, 2024]
  [Previous Article 12-2 moved to Article 12-3 <2024. 4. 16.>]

Article 12-3 (Registration of Lifelong Education Facilities for Persons with Disabilities) (1) "Facilities and equipment prescribed by Presidential Decree" in Article 20-2 (2) of the Act mean facilities and equipment according to the criteria prescribed in Appendix 1-2. <Amended on Dec. 9, 2021>
  (2) Any person who intends to register a lifelong education facility for persons with disabilities referred to in Article 20-2 (1) of the Act (hereinafter referred to as "lifelong education facility for persons with disabilities") pursuant to paragraph (2) of that Article shall submit a registration application describing the following matters to the superintendent of education together with the operation regulations of the relevant facility and documents determined and publicly notified by the superintendent of education:
  1. Name;
  2. Type and purpose;
  3. Location;
  4. Details concerning organization of curriculum;
  5. Matters related to expenses (including matters related to tuition fees, if tuition fees are paid) and the methods for maintaining the relevant facility;
  6. Plans for installation of facilities and equipment;
  7. Date on which such establishment is planned to open.
  (3) The operation regulations referred to in paragraph (2) shall prescribe matters related to the following:
  1. Name, type, purpose, and location;
  2. Curricula and the maximum number;
  3. Admission and discharge;
  4. The period of education and cancellation of classes;
  5. Tuition fees (limited to cases where tuition fees are paid);
  6. Other matters necessary for operation.
  (4) 　Upon receiving the registration application referred to in paragraph (2), the superintendent of education shall review it and issue a registration certificate prescribed by Decree of the Ministry of Education to the applicant if such application meets the registration requirements.
  [This Article Added on May 29, 2017]
  [Moved from Article 12-2; Previous Article 12-3 moved to Article 12-6 <Apr. 16, 2024>]

Article 12-4 (Registration of modification of registration of lifelong education facilities for persons with disabilities) Where a person who has registered a lifelong educational establishment for persons with disabilities under Article 20-2 (2) of the Act intends to modify matters falling under the operational rules under Article 12-3 (2) with the exception of its subparagraphs or any of the subparagraphs of Article 12-3 (2) pursuant to Article 38-2 (1) of the Act, he or she shall file for registration of modification with the superintendent of education.
  [This Article Added on Apr. 16, 2024]

Article 12-5 (Report on closure of lifelong education facilities for persons with disabilities) The Article 20-2 (3) of the Act, a person who intends to close a lifelong educational establishment for persons with disabilities pursuant to Article 20-2 (3) of the Act shall file a report thereon with the superintendent of education by no later than 30 days before the scheduled date of closure, along with documents stating the following matters:
  1. Grounds for closure;
  2. Date of closure;
  3. Methods of handling remaining business affairs.
  [This Article Added on Apr. 16, 2024]

Article 12-6 (Subsidization of Expenses for Operating Lifelong Education Facilities for Persons with Disabilities) The state and local governments may support the following expenses to lifelong education facilities for the disabled pursuant to Article 20-2 (4) of the Act. <Amended on Apr. 16, 2024>
  1. Expenses incurred in renovating or repairing facilities and equipment;
  2. Personnel expenses for operating facilities;
  3. Expenses for providing meals and snacks to facility users;
  4. Expenses incurred in conducting lifelong education for persons with disabilities, including the expenses for purchasing textbooks and teaching materials;
  5. Where education for persons with disabilities prescribed in other statutes or regulations, such as education prescribed in Article 10 (2) of the Act on Guarantee of Rights of and Support for Persons with Developmental Disabilities, is conducted at lifelong education facilities for persons with disabilities, expenses incurred in providing such education;
  6. Other expenses incurred in operating lifelong education facilities for persons with disabilities.
  [This Article Added on May 29, 2017]
  [Moved from Article 12-3 <Apr. 16, 2024>]

Article 13 (Operation of professional human resources information bank system) (1) The Minister of Education and the heads of local governments may operate a system (hereinafter referred to as "professional human resources information bank system") designed to collect, provide and manage information concerning lecturers under Article 22 (2) of the Act. <Amended on Feb. 29, 2008; Mar. 23, 2013>
  (2) Collection, provision, and management of information under paragraph (1) shall be limited to cases where the principal agrees.
  (3) The Minister of Education and the heads of local governments may entrust operation of the professional human resources information bank system to the National Institute for Lifelong Education or City/Do institute. <Amended on Feb. 29, 2008; Mar. 23, 2013>
  (4) Matters necessary for the scope, etc. of information under paragraph (1) shall be prescribed by Decree of the Ministry of Education. <Amended on Feb. 29, 2008; Mar. 23, 2013>

Article 14 (Operation of study record system) (1) The Minister of Education may operate a study record system under Article 23 (1) of the Act. <Amended on Feb. 29, 2008; Aug. 11, 2009; Mar. 23, 2013>
  (2) The study record system under paragraph (1) shall be established only when the principal or a person entrusted by the principal applies for it. <Amended on Dec. 20, 2010>
  (3) Any person who intends to inspect information contained in a study record system under paragraph (1) or to have a certificate issued may file an application thereof with the Minister of Education. In such cases, such application for inspection of information or for the issuance of such certificate shall be made only by the principal or another person entrusted by him or her. <Amended on Feb. 29, 2008; Mar. 23, 2013>
  (4) The Minister of Education may entrust operation of a study record system to the National Institute for Lifelong Education. <Amended on Feb. 29, 2008; Mar. 23, 2013>
  (5) Matters necessary for the scope, etc. of information to be entered in a study record system under paragraph (1) shall be prescribed by Decree of the Ministry of Education. <Amended on Feb. 29, 2008; Mar. 23, 2013>
  (6) The Minister of Education (including those who are entrusted with the operation of a study record system pursuant to paragraph (4)) may manage data including resident registration numbers under subparagraph 1 of Article 19 of the Enforcement Decree of the Personal Information Protection Act where unavoidable to perform the duties of inspecting information contained in the study record system and issuing certificates. <Added on on Jan. Jan. 6, 2012; Mar. 23, 2013>

Article 14-2 (Evaluation and accreditation) (1) A lifelong educational institution that intends to receive the evaluation and accreditation for a studying course pursuant to Article 23 (2) of the Act (hereinafter referred to as "evaluation and accreditation") shall submit an evaluation and accreditation application form and relevant documents to the Minister of Education as prescribed by Decree of the Ministry of Education. <Amended on Mar. 23, 2013>
  (2) Criteria for evaluation and accreditation shall be as follows. In such case, the Minister of Education may apply the criteria to the evaluation and accreditation by subdividing them, in consideration of the characteristics of the subjects of evaluation and accreditation: <Amended on Mar. 23, 2013>
  1. Educational facilities and installations;
  2. Curricula;
  3. Faculties and lecturers;
  4. System for supporting and managing learners;
  5. Other matters recognized by the Minister of Education to be necessary for the operation of studying courses.
  (3) Where the Minister of Education conducts evaluation and accreditation, he or she shall determine detailed matters necessary for the evaluation and accreditation, such as criteria, subject, procedure, and method, and publicly announce them one month prior to the date of receipt of evaluation and accreditation application forms. <Amended on Mar. 23, 2013>
  (4) The Minister of Education shall examine whether a studying course for which an application is made for evaluation and accreditation pursuant to paragraph (1) conforms to the criteria in paragraph (2) and shall notify the applicant of the result thereof. <Amended on Mar. 23, 2013>
  (5) The validity of evaluation and accreditation shall be five years from the date on which a notice of evaluation and accreditation is received.
  (6) Other than those prescribed in paragraphs (1) through (5), matters necessary for procedures for and methods of evaluation and accreditation and modification of evaluation and accreditation shall be determined by Decree of the Ministry of Education. <Amended on Mar. 23, 2013>
  [This Article Wholly Amended on Dec. 20, 2010]

Article 14-3 (Recognition of credits or educational attainment) Where a learner intends to obtain recognition of credits or academic background as a result of completing a course of study evaluated and certified pursuant to Article 23 (2) of the Act pursuant to paragraph (3) of that Article, Articles 7 and 8 of the Act on Recognition of Credits shall apply to the procedures, methods, etc. for such recognition. In such cases, a learner may utilize the credits or academic background recognized pursuant to the former part of this Article for the acquisition of qualifications, as prescribed by statutes or regulations.
  [This Article Added on Apr. 16, 2024]
  [Previous Article 14-3 moved to Article 14-4 <Apr. 16, 2024>]

Article 14-4 (Corrective Orders to Lifelong Educational Institutions) (1) When the Minister of Education issues a correction order to a lifelong education institution pursuant to Article 23 (5) of the Act, he or she shall order the correction within a period of not more than two months. <Amended on Dec. 20, 2010; Mar. 23, 2013; Apr. 16, 2024>
  (2) A lifelong educational institution subject to a corrective order under paragraph (1) shall without delay perform such order and report the results thereof to the Minister of Education. <Amended on Dec. 20, 2010; Mar. 23, 2013>
  (3) Where it is obvious that damage to learners will continue to be caused by a lifelong educational institution in violation of Article 23 (4) 2 or 3 of the Act, the Minister of Education may publicly announce the fact that a corrective order has been issued and the details thereof on its website. <Amended on Dec. 20, 2010; Mar. 23, 2013; Apr. 16, 2024>
  (4) Any person who has an objection to the corrective order under paragraph (1) may raise an application for the objection to the Minister of Education within 15 days from the date on which such notice was received, stating the reasons for objection, contents, etc., with the relevant documents, and the Minister of Education shall, if no special reason exists to the contrary, examine such application within 30 days and notify the applicant of the results thereof. <Amended on Mar. 23, 2013>
  (5) When a lifelong educational institution raises an objection pursuant to paragraph (4), the period of carrying out the order for correction in paragraph (1) shall be considered to be extended as long as the number of days during the period starting from the date on which the objection is raised to the date on which a notice of the result thereof is given. <Added on on Dec. Dec. 20, 2010>
  [This Article Added on Aug. 11, 2009]
  [Moved from Article 14-3, and the previous Article 14-4 moved to Article 14-5 <Apr. 16, 2024>]

Article 14-5 (Public Announcement of Evaluation and Accreditation) When the Minister of Education intends to conduct evaluation and accreditation or revoke evaluation and accreditation pursuant to Article 23 (4) of the Act, he or she shall publicly announce the details thereof by posting them on the website. <Amended on Dec. 20, 2010; Mar. 23, 2013; Apr. 16, 2024>
  [This Article Added on Aug. 11, 2009]
  [Moved from Article 14-4 <Apr. 16, 2024>]

CHAPTER IV CERTIFIED LIFELONG EDUCATION TEACHERS

Article 15 (Other qualifications of certified lifelong education teachers) "Any person who has other qualifications prescribed by Presidential Decree" in Article 24 (1) 4 of the Act means a person who has the qualification requirements for each grade as listed in Appendix 1-3 and who has not been prescribed in Article 24 (1) 1 through 3 of the Act: <Amended on Aug. 11, 2009; May 29, 2017; Dec. 9, 2021>
  1. Deleted; <Aug. 11, 2009>
  2. Deleted; <Aug. 11, 2009>
  3. Deleted. <Aug. 11, 2009>

Article 16 (Grades of certified lifelong education teachers) (1) Certified lifelong education teachers under Article 24 (4) of the Act shall be classified into Grade I, Grade II, and Grade III.
  (2) The qualification requirements for each grade of certified lifelong education teachers under paragraph (1) shall be specified in Appendix 1-3. <Amended on May 29, 2017; Dec. 9, 2021>

Article 17 (Scope of duties) Certified lifelong education teachers shall perform the following duties for the promotion of lifelong education under Article 24 (4) of the Act:
  1. Request analysis, development, operation, evaluation and consulting of lifelong education programs;
  2. Provision of study information, counselling of career capability development and teaching to learners;
  3. Other duties, such as business plans related to the promotion of lifelong education.

Article 18 (Study courses) (1) Study courses under Article 24 (4) of the Act shall be divided into courses for training and courses for promotion.
  (2) The Minister of Education may entrust the operation of courses for training and courses for promotion under paragraph (1) to the National Institute for Lifelong Education or an educational institution designated by Article 25 (1) of the Act. <Amended on Feb. 29, 2008; Mar. 23, 2013>

Article 19 (Training) (1) The president of the National Institute for Lifelong Education and the president of a City/Do institute (hereinafter referred to as the "head of the training institution") may conduct a training for certified lifelong education teachers under Article 24 (4) of the Act; provided, if deemed necessary by the head of the training institution, such training may be entrusted to an institution specializing in lifelong education.
  (2) The State and local governments may subsidize the part of costs incurred in the training for certified lifelong education teachers under paragraph (1) to the head of the training institution.

Article 20 (Procedures for issuance of certificates for certified lifelong education teachers) (1) Any person who intends to have a certificate for certified lifelong education teachers under Article 24 (4) of the Act issued shall file an application for issuance of a certificate for certified lifelong education teachers, accompanied by documents prescribed by Decree of the Ministry of Education, with the Minister of Education. <Amended on Feb. 29, 2008; Mar. 23, 2013>
  (2) Any person who intends to have a certificate for certified lifelong education teachers re-issued due to the loss, damage or alternation of entries of such certificate shall file an application for re-issuance of a certificate for certified lifelong education teachers, accompanied by documents prescribed by Decree of the Ministry of Education, with the Minister of Education. <Amended on Feb. 29, 2008; Mar. 23, 2013>

Article 21 (Designation of training institutions for certified lifelong education teachers) (1) Lifelong educational institutions that can be designated as a training institution for certified lifelong education teachers under Article 25 of the Act shall be institutions falling under any of the following: <Amended on Feb. 3, 2016>
  1. A lifelong educational establishment affiliated with a university under Article 30 (2) of the Act;
  2. An educational and training institution for public officials under the Act on the Capacity Development of Public Officials;
  3. A training institution under the Educational Officials Act;
  4. A training and educational institution established under any special Act, or as a government-funded institution.
  (2) Any person who intends to have his or her institution designated as a training institution for certified lifelong education teachers under Article 25 of the Act shall file an application for designation of a training institution for certified lifelong education teachers, stating the matters falling under each of the following, accompanied by documents prescribed by Decree of the Ministry of Education, with the Minister of Education: <Amended on Feb. 29, 2008; Mar. 23, 2013>
  1. Name;
  2. Objectives;
  3. Location;
  4. Name and address of representative;
  5. Date on which such institution is planned to open.
  (3) Upon receipt of an application for designation under paragraph (2), the Minister of Education shall determine whether to grant such designation, taking into account the facilities, human resources, curricula, location, etc. of the institution subject to such designation, and where he or she decides to grant such designation, issue to the applicant a certificate of designation prescribed by Decree of the Ministry of Education. <Amended on Feb. 29, 2008; Mar. 23, 2013>

Article 22 (Institutions subject to placement of certified lifelong education teachers and standards for placement) Institutions in which certified lifelong education teachers will be placed and standards for the placement under Article 26 (4) of the Act shall be specified in Appendix 2.

Article 22-2 (Status survey) (1) Fact-finding surveys on certified lifelong education teachers under Article 26-2 of the Act (hereinafter referred to as "fact-finding survey") shall include the following matters:
  1. Matters concerning the current status of training and placement of certified lifelong education teachers;
  2. Matters concerning the level of remuneration and payment status of lifelong educators;
  3. Matters concerning current status of activities and services of certified lifelong education teachers;
  4. Other matters the Minister of Education deems necessary to ascertain the actual conditions of certified lifelong education teachers.
  (2) Fact-finding surveys shall be conducted by means of field surveys, written surveys, statistical surveys, etc., and may be conducted by electronic means, such as information and communications networks or electronic mail, in order to efficiently conduct fact-finding surveys.
  (3) The Minister of Education may request a research institute, corporation, organization, or related expert with expertise in lifelong education to conduct a fact-finding survey.
  (4) Where necessary to conduct a fact-finding survey, the Minister of Education may request the establisher and operator of a lifelong educational institution, the head of a relevant central administrative agency, the head of a local government, or the head of a relevant institution or organization to submit materials or state opinions.
  [This Article Added on Apr. 16, 2024]

CHAPTER V LIFELONG EDUCATIONAL INSTITUTIONS

Article 23 (Return of tuition fees) Where any ground for return of tuition fees prescribed in Article 28 (4) of the Act occurs, the founder or operator of a lifelong educational institution shall return tuitions fees to learners within five days from the date when such ground occurs in accordance with the standards for return prescribed in Appendix 3.
  [This Article Wholly Amended on Aug. 2, 2016]

Article 23-2 (Evaluation and certification of lifelong education institutions) (1) The standards for the evaluation or certification of lifelong educational institutions under Article 28-2 (1) of the Act shall be as follows:
  1. Suitability of expansion and management of educational facilities, equipment and human resources;
  2. Records of systematicity and specialization of planning and operation of curricula;
  3. Other matters deemed necessary by the minister of education for evaluation or certification of lifelong educational institutions by the minister of education.
  (2) The standards for the evaluation or certification of curricula under Article 28-2 (1) of the Act shall be as follows:
  1. Records of systematicity and specialization of planning and operation of curricula;
  2. Other matters that the Minister of Education deems necessary for the evaluation or certification of curricula.
  (3) Where the Minister of Education finds that a lifelong educational institution or educational course meets the standards prescribed in paragraph (1) or (2) as a result of evaluating the lifelong educational institution or educational course pursuant to Article 28-2 of the Act, he or she shall issue a certificate to the lifelong educational institution which has applied for evaluation and certification, as determined and publicly notified by the Minister of Education.
  (4) A lifelong educational institution issued with a certificate pursuant to paragraph (3) may indicate the fact and details of the relevant certification on outdoor signboards, various documents, promotional materials, the website of such institution, etc.
  (5) Pursuant to Article 28-2 (2) of the Act, the Minister of Education may entrust affairs concerning the operation and management of evaluation or certification [including affairs concerning the issuance of a certificate under paragraph (3) (referring to a certificate in the name of the Minister of Education)] to the following institutions or organizations:
  1. Promotion Agency;
  2. Institutions or Organizations recognized by the Minister of Education as having human and material resources capable of performing affairs concerning evaluation or certification.
  (6) Where the Minister of Education entrusts affairs pursuant to paragraph (5), he or she shall publicly announce the institutions or organizations to which the affairs are entrusted and the details of the affairs entrusted on the website of the Ministry of Education.
  (7) Except as otherwise expressly provided for in paragraphs (1) through (6), detailed matters concerning the procedures and methods for the evaluation or certification of lifelong educational institutions and educational courses, such as applications for evaluation or certification, shall be determined and publicly notified by the Minister of Education.
  [This Article Added on Apr. 16, 2024]

Article 24 (Report on establishment of lifelong educational establishments affiliated with schools) The heads of various levels of schools who establish lifelong educational establishments affiliated with schools under Article 30 (1) of the Act shall file a report determined by Decree of the Ministry of Education to the jurisdictional authority, accompanied by operational regulations. The same shall also apply where the reported matters are changed. <Amended on Feb. 29, 2008; Mar. 23, 2013>

Article 25 (Facilities and equipment of school-type lifelong educational establishments) (1) "Facilities and equipment prescribed by Presidential Decree" in Article 31 (1) of the Act means facilities and equipment falling under the following:
  1. Study facilities and equipment;
  2. Data room;
  3. Management office.
  (2) Detailed standards for the facilities and equipment under paragraph (1) shall be prescribed by Decree of the Ministry of Education. <Amended on Feb. 29, 2008; Mar. 23, 2013>

Article 26 (Registration of school-type lifelong educational establishments) (1) Any person who intends to establish and operate a school-type lifelong education establishment under Article 31 (1) of the Act shall file an application for registration stating matters falling under each of the following with the superintendent of education, accompanied by operational regulations and documents prescribed by Decree of the Ministry of Education: <Amended on Feb. 29, 2008; Mar. 23, 2013>
  1. Name;
  2. Objectives;
  3. Location;
  4. Compilation of curricula;
  5. Expenses, including tuition fees, and the method of maintaining facilities;
  6. Plans for installation of facilities and equipment;
  7. Date on which such establishment is planned to open.
  (2) Matters falling under each of the following shall be entered in the operational regulations under paragraph (1):
  1. Name, objectives and location;
  2. Curricula and the maximum number;
  3. Admission, expulsion, the completion of a course of study, award and punishment;
  4. Recognition of the completion of the course of study;
  5. Educational period and vacation;
  6. Tuition fees;
  7. Other matters necessary for operation.
  (3) Upon receipt of an application for registration under paragraph (1), the superintendent of education shall examine the application and, where such application is found to satisfy requirements for registration, he or she shall issue to the applicant a registration certificate prescribed by Decree of the Ministry of Education. <Amended on Feb. 29, 2008; Mar. 23, 2013>

Article 26-2 (Registration of modification of facilities of school-type lifelong educational establishments) Where a person who has registered facilities of a school-type lifelong educational establishment under Article 31 (1) of the Act intends to modify the following matters pursuant to Article 38-2 (1) of the Act, he or she shall register such modifications with the superintendent of education:
  1. Name;
  2. Location;
  3. Formulation of educational curricula;
  4. Expenses including tuition fees and methods of maintaining establishments;
  5. Details of installing establishments and equipment;
  6. Operational rules (excluding modification of purposes).
  [This Article Added on Jun. 30, 2014]

Article 27 (Standards for designation of establishments, graduates of which are recognized as having educational attainment) (1) Standards for designating a lifelong educational establishment, the graduates of which are recognized as having educational attainment and a degree equal to those of graduates of a high school or lower under the main clause of Article 31 (2) of the Act and paragraph (5) of that Article (hereinafter referred to as "establishment, the graduates of which are recognized as having educational attainment") shall conform to the standards for establishing and operating various schools corresponding to elementary schools, middle schools or high schools (referring to schools under subparagraph 5 of Article 2 of the Elementary and Secondary Education Act; hereinafter the same shall apply) with respect to the following matters, except for matters prescribed in paragraphs (2) through (6): <Amended on Nov. 26, 2015; Mar. 25, 2016>
  1. Term of study, semester, number of school days and number of school hours;
  2. Curricula;
  3. Maximum number of students, number of classes, and organization of classes;
  4. Admission qualifications;
  5. Qualifications and maximum number of teachers;
  6. Completion of the course of study and graduation;
  7. Facilities and equipment;
  8. Text books and teaching materials;
  9. Regulations on finance and accounting.
  (2) The semesters referred to in paragraph (1) 1 may be operated by dividing each school year into three semesters with approval from the competent authority. In such cases, the term of school years shall be reduced by up to two years for elementary school courses and one year for middle school and high school courses, but a person who may be admitted to the reduced high school courses shall be any of the following persons from among those who meet the admission requirements referred to in paragraph (3): <Amended on Apr. 16, 2024>
  1. Person over 16 years of age;
  2. Those who stop studying due to reasons, such as expulsion from school after admission to a high school;
  3. Minors who work for an industrial enterprise.
  (3) In cases of an elementary school curriculum among the admission qualifications referred to in paragraph (1) 4, it shall be a person who has not received elementary education and is in excess of the school age provided for in Article 13 (1) of the Elementary and Secondary Education Act; in cases of a middle school, it shall be a person who has the admission qualifications for the middle school under Article 43 (1) of the Elementary and Secondary Education Act and is in excess of the school age provided for in Article 13 (3) of the Elementary and Secondary Education Act; and in cases of a high school, it shall be a person who has the admission qualifications for the high school under Article 47 (1) the Elementary and Secondary Education Act.
  (4) An assistant principal among teachers referred to in paragraph (1) 5 may not be appointed and in cases of operating an elementary school curriculum, one teacher other than the principal and the assistant principal shall be posted in every class. In cases of less than six classes, the principal and the assistant principle may take charge of classes, and in cases of less than twelve classes, the assistant principal may take charge of a class.
  (5) The standard area of a gymnasium among facilities and equipment of paragraph (1) 7 shall be not less than 350 square meters, but such gymnasium may be substituted by an indoor sports facility equal in area to such gymnasium; provided, a gymnasium may not be established where the establishment falls under Article 5 (3) 1 or 2 of the Regulations on the Establishment and Operation of Schools of Various Levels Equal to or Lower than High School.
  (6) Any educational establishment, the graduates of which are recognized as having educational attainment, which operates simultaneously elementary and middle school curricula, middle and high school curricula, or elementary, middle and high school curricula, may be governed by the following standards: <Amended on Jul. 2, 2019>
  1. Standards for facilities and equipment (excluding standards for teaching aids and books) may be governed by standards for establishing and operating various schools equivalent to the various levels of schools, among the schools which are operated simultaneously, and a gymnasium, management office, special classrooms, etc. may be used jointly;
  2. Teaching aids and books shall be secured by subject and curriculum under Article 8 of the Regulations on the Establishment and Operation of Schools of Various Levels Equal to or Lower than High School and they may be jointly used within the scope of not hindering studying and teaching;
  3. One person may be the principal of all schools and teachers may simultaneously teach only in middle school and high school curricula within the scope of not hindering teaching.
  [Article 27 (2) 1, applicable from Feb. 15, 2011]

Article 28 (Application for designation of establishments, graduates of which are recognized as having educational attainment) (1) Any person who intends to have his or her establishment recognized as an establishment, the graduates of which are recognized as having educational attainment under the main clause of Article 31 (2) of the Act and paragraph (5) of that Article shall file an application for designation of an establishment, the graduates of which are recognized as having educational attainment with the superintendent of education, stating the matters falling under each of the following, accompanied by documents prescribed by Decree of the Ministry of Education: <Amended on Feb. 29, 2008; Mar. 23, 2013; Mar. 25, 2016>
  1. Name;
  2. Objectives;
  3. Location;
  4. Number of classes by the course of study, the maximum number, and tuition fees;
  5. Compilation of curriculum;
  6. The maximum number of teachers;
  7. Plans for securing necessary expenses;
  8. Current facilities and plans for expansion of facilities;
  9. Current conditions of teaching tools and other equipment, and plans for expansion of equipment;
  10. Date on which such establishment is planned to open.
  (2) Upon receipt of an application for designation under paragraph (1), the superintendent of education shall examine comprehensively standards for designation and educational conditions of the region, such as the prospect of supply and demand of the students of a regular school, shall decide whether to grant such designation, and may issue to the applicant a certificate of designation prescribed by Decree of the Ministry of Education. <Amended on Feb. 29, 2008; Mar. 23, 2013>

Article 28-2 (Standards for revocation of designation of establishments, graduates of which are recognized as having educational attainment) (1) In any of the following cases, the superintendent of education may revoke the designation of an establishment, the graduates of which are recognized as having educational attainment pursuant to the proviso to Article 31 (2) of the Act:
  1. When the sum of subsidies that the founder or operator of an establishment, the graduates of which are recognized as having educational attainment has used for any purpose other than their intended ones or executed by any unjust means, by intention, falls under any of the following:
    (a) On the basis of the annual sum (referring to the period from January 1 to December 31 of the relevant year: hereafter in this paragraph, the same shall apply): At least 100 million won, or at least 30 percent of the total amount of subsidies for the relevant year;
    (b) On the basis of the accumulated sum: At least 300 million won;
  2. When the sum of subsidies that the founder and operator of an establishment, the graduates of which are recognized as having educational attainment has used for any purpose other than their intended ones or executed by any unjust means, by intention or negligence, falls under any of the following:
    (a) On the basis of the annual sum: At least 200 million won, or at least 50 percent of the total amount of subsidies for the relevant year;
    (b) On the basis of the accumulated sum: At least 600 million won.
  (2) Where the superintendent of education intends to revoke the designation of an establishment, the graduates of which are recognized as having educational attainment under the proviso to Article 31 (2) of the Act, he or she shall hold a hearing.
  (3) Where the superintendent of education revokes the designation of an establishment, the graduates of which are recognized as having educational attainment under the proviso to Article 31 (2) of the Act, he or she shall manage the school register to be submitted by the relevant establishment. In such cases, matters necessary for managing school registers shall be determined by the superintendent of education.
  (4) Where the superintendent of education revokes the designation of an establishment, the graduates of which are recognized as having educational attainment under the proviso to Article 31 (2) of the Act, he or she shall take measures for protecting the enrolled students’ right for learning, such as introducing other establishments, the graduates of which are recognized as having educational attainment to them.
  [This Article Added on Mar. 25, 2016]

Article 29 (Authorization for closure of establishments, graduates of which are recognized as having educational attainment) (1) Article 31 (7) of the Act, a person who intends to close an establishment subject to recognition of educational attainment under Article 31 (2) of the Act shall obtain authorization from the superintendent of education, along with documents stating the following matters: <Amended on Apr. 16, 2024>
  1. Grounds for closure;
  2. Date of closure;
  3. Student protection measures;
  4. Methods of handling school register, remaining business affairs and property.
  (2) The management of school registers of an establishment, the graduates of which are recognized as having educational attainment which has been closed under paragraph (1) shall be governed by the superintendent of education.

Article 30 (Standards for authorization for lifelong educational establishments, graduates of which are recognized as having educational attainment and degree equal to those of junior colleges) Where a high technical school which establishes and operates a specialized department pursuant to Article 54 (4) of the Elementary and Secondary Education Act intends to obtain authorization for converting it to a lifelong educational establishment, the graduates of which are recognized as having educational attainment and a degree equal to those of graduates of a junior college under Article 31 (4) or (5) of the Act (hereinafter referred to as "lifelong educational establishment, the graduates of which are recognized as having educational attainment and a degree equal to those of graduates of a junior college"), it shall satisfy all the following requirements: <Amended on Aug. 9, 2022>
  1. It shall be a school corporation;
  2. It shall secure a school site under Article 30-2. In such cases, provisions regarding the standard school building area per student stipulated in Appendix 6 shall apply to matters regarding the standard school building area;
  3. It shall secure school buildings under Article 40;
  4. It shall secure at least 1/2 of the number of teachers required to be secured under Article 41 (hereinafter referred to as "statutory number of teachers"). In such cases, it may have up to half the statutory number of teachers concurrently serve as teachers, and the rest of teachers other than those secured at the time of authorization for establishment shall be secured within one year after it opens after conversion;
  5. It shall secure the basis property for generating revenues pursuant to the classification of the following items:
    (a) If the maximum number of students is not less than 1,000: 10 billion won or more;
    (b) If the maximum number of students is not less than 500: 7 billion won or more;
    (c) If the maximum number of students is less than 500: 4 billion or more.

Article 30-2 (School sites of lifelong educational establishment, graduates of which are recognized as having educational attainment and degree equal to those of graduates of junior college) (1) A lifelong educational establishment, the graduates of which are recognized as having educational attainment and a degree equal to those of graduates of a junior college, shall secure a school site meeting the standard areas specified in Appendix 3-2 in appropriate places without impediment to education and research activities. In such cases, if the site of the same lifelong educational establishment is divided, it shall meet the standard areas referred to in Appendix 3-2 based on the maximum number of students accommodated by respective school sites.
  (2) Where the school site of a lifelong educational establishment, the graduates of which are recognized as having educational attainment and a degree equal to those of graduates of a junior college, falls under any of the following subparagraphs, the latter part of paragraph (1) shall not apply, deeming that the school site is not divided:
  1. Where the school sites are adjoined, being unavoidably divided by road, river, etc.;
  2. Where the shortest distance between school sites based on the boundary line of the school sites (where a school site is deemed not to be divided, including the boundary line of the relevant school site) is not more than two kilometers;
  3. Where a lifelong educational establishment, the graduates of which are recognized as having educational attainment and a degree equal to those of graduates of a junior college, establishes a student welfare facility (limited to student residence facilities including dormitories; hereafter in this Article the same shall apply) among support facilities of in-house college school buildings provided in Appendix 5 outside the existing school site (where the existing school sites are already divided, referring to the school site nearest to the student welfare facility);
  (3) The school sites prescribed in paragraph (1) shall exclude the following sites from among all sites used by a lifelong educational establishment, the graduates of which are recognized as having educational attainment and a degree equal to those of graduates of a junior college:
  1. Hands-on training sites, such as farms, scientific forests, breeding farms, ranches, fishing grounds, and herb gardens;
  2. A site for a facility or building used as a student welfare facility among the support facilities of in-house college school buildings prescribed in Appendix 5, which is not owned by a person who has obtained authorization to convert to a lifelong educational establishment, the graduates of which are recognized as having educational attainment and a degree equal to those of graduates of a junior college;
  3. A site constituting a basis property used for generating revenues under subparagraph 5 of Article 30.
  [This Article Added on Aug. 9, 2022]

Article 31 (Authorization for establishment of lifelong educational establishments, graduates of which are recognized as having educational attainment and degree equal to those of graduates of junior college) (1) Any person who intends to obtain authorization for the establishment of a lifelong educational establishment, graduates of which are recognized as having educational attainment and a degree equal to those of graduates of a junior college pursuant to Article 31 (4) and (5) of the Act, shall submit to the Minister of Education an establishment plan for a lifelong educational establishment, graduates of which are recognized as having educational attainment and a degree equal to those of graduates of a junior college, where the following matters shall be entered, together with the documents prescribed by Decree of the Ministry of Education: <Amended on Feb. 29, 2008; Mar. 23, 2013; Jun. 30, 2014>
  1. Name;
  2. Objectives;
  3. A person who establishes such distance college-type educational establishment;
  4. Location;
  5. School regulations;
  6. Financial management plans for the next two years;
  7. Plans for securing facilities and equipment for education and research for the next two years;
  8. Plans for securing facilities and equipment used for teaching practice if such teaching practice is required;
  9. Plans for securing teachers;
  10. Date on which the establishment is planned to open after conversion.
  (2) The name under paragraph (1) 1 shall include the term to represent the objectives of establishment of the relevant school and characteristics of the major field of the relevant school.
  (3) Article 4 (1) of the Enforcement Decree of the Higher Education Act shall apply mutatis mutandis to entries of the school regulations.
  (4) Upon receipt of a plan for establishment of a lifelong educational establishment, the graduates of which are recognized as having educational attainment and a degree equal to those of graduates of a junior college under paragraph (1), the Minister of Education shall deal with such plan by applying mutatis mutandis to the procedures under Article 36 (4) through (8) other than the application and period of treatment. <Amended on Feb. 29, 2008; Oct. 20, 2008; Mar. 23, 2013>

Article 31-2 (Authorization for modification of lifelong educational establishments, graduates of which are recognized as having educational attainment and degree equal to those of graduates of junior college) Where any person who has obtained authorization for the establishment of a lifelong educational establishment, graduates of which are recognized as having educational attainment equivalent to that of a graduate of a junior college under Article 31 (4) and (5) intends to modify matters referred to in Article 31 (1) 1 through 4, as prescribed in Article 38-2 (1) of the Act, he or she shall obtain authorization for such modification from the Minister of Education. <Amended on Nov. 26, 2015>
  [This Article Added on Jun. 30, 2014]

Article 32 (Authorization for closure of lifelong educational establishments, graduates of which are recognized as having educational attainment and degree equal to those of graduates of junior colleges) (1) Article 31 (7) of the Act, a person who intends to close a lifelong educational establishment subject to recognition of educational attainment of a junior college pursuant to Article 31 (7) of the Act shall obtain authorization from the Minister of Education, along with documents stating the following matters: <Amended on Feb. 29, 2008; Mar. 23, 2013; Apr. 16, 2024>
  1. Grounds for closure;
  2. Date of closure;
  3. Student protection measures;
  4. Methods of handling school register, remaining business affairs and property.
  (2) The management of the register of any lifelong educational establishment, the graduates of which are recognized as having educational attainment and a degree equal to those of graduates of a junior college that has been closed under paragraph (1) shall be governed by the Minister of Education. <Amended on Feb. 29, 2008; Mar. 23, 2013>

Article 33 (Operational methods of credit system of lifelong educational establishments, graduates of which are recognized as having educational attainment and degree equal to those of graduates of junior colleges) Articles 42 through 44 shall apply mutatis mutandis to the amendment to the school regulations, school year, semester, curriculum, etc. of any lifelong educational establishment, the graduates of which are recognized as having educational attainment and a degree equal to those of graduates of a junior college, and Articles 61 and 63 shall apply mutatis mutandis to tuition fees and finance and accounting of such establishment.

Article 33-2 (Education Entrusted to Industrial Establishments Established by Lifelong Educational Establishments Subject to Recognition of Educational Attainment of Junior Colleges) (1) Lifelong Educational Establishments Subject to Recognition of Educational Attainment of Junior Colleges may provide education entrusted by industrial enterprises (including organizations comprised of industrial enterprises) with recognition of educational attainment of junior colleges.
  (2) Article 53-2 of the Enforcement Decree of the Higher Education Act shall apply mutatis mutandis to entrusted education under paragraph (1).
  [This Article Added on Dec. 13, 2024]

Article 34 (Other statutes or regulations applicable mutatis mutandis) Except as provided in this Decree, the provisions on junior colleges referred to in the Higher Education Act shall apply mutatis mutandis to the establishment and operation of lifelong educational establishments, the graduates of which are recognized as having educational attainment and a degree equal to those of graduates of junior colleges.

Article 35 (Scope of place of business) Places of Business (including jointly participating places of business) of at least the scale prescribed by Presidential Decree in Article 32 (1) 1 of the Act means a place of business where the number of employees (including employees employed by the relevant place of business and employees of other companies working in the relevant place of business) working at a place of business which is a corporation established under the Commercial Act or special Act is at least 200. <Amended on Apr. 16, 2024>
  [This Article Wholly Amended on Aug. 11, 2009]

Article 36 (Authorization for establishment of in-house colleges) (1) Any person who intends to establish and operate a lifelong educational establishment in the form of an in-house college (hereinafter referred to as "in-house college") under Article 32 (1) of the Act shall file a plan for establishing an in-house college, stating the following matters, accompanied by documents prescribed by Decree of the Ministry of Education, with the Minister of Education, by nine months prior to the opening of such in-house college: <Amended on Feb. 29, 2008; Aug. 11, 2009; Mar. 23, 2013>
  1. Name;
  2. Objectives;
  3. A person who establishes such distance college-type educational establishment;
  4. Location;
  5. Operational regulations (hereafter in this Article through Article 46 referred to as "school regulations");
  6. Financial management plans for the next four years (two years, in cases of an in-house college that operates a two-year bachelor course or an in-house college whose educational attainment and degree are recognized as equal to those of graduates of a junior college);
  7. Plans for securing facilities and equipment used to conduct education and research for the next four years (two years, in cases of an in-house college that operates a two-year bachelor course or an in-house college whose educational attainment and degree are recognized as equal to those of graduates of a junior college);
  8. Plans for securing facilities and equipment used for teaching practice if such teaching practice is required;
  9. Plans for securing teachers;
  10. Date on which the in-house college is planned to open.
  (2) The name under paragraph (1) 1 shall be the words signifying an in-house college.
  (3) Article 4 (1) of the Enforcement Decree of the Higher Education Act shall apply mutatis mutandis to entries of the school regulations.
  (4) Upon receipt of a plan for establishing an in-house college, etc. referred to in paragraph (1), the Minister of Education shall determine whether approval should be granted after gathering consensus of the specialists, and notify the applicant of the results thereof within three months from the date on which the application is filed; provided, the Minister of Education deems it necessary to consult with government ministries and agencies concerned about the relevant authorization, he or she may notify the applicant of the results thereof within six months from the date on which the application is filed. <Amended on Feb. 29, 2008; Oct. 20, 2008; Mar. 23, 2013>
  (5) Any applicant who has been served with a notice on approval of his or her plan for establishing an in-house college under paragraph (4) shall install facilities and equipment according to such plan and file an application for authorizing the establishment of such in-house college with the Minister of Education by six months prior to the opening of such in-house college. <Amended on Feb. 29, 2008; Mar. 23, 2013>
  (6) Upon receipt of an application for authorizing the establishment of an in-house college under paragraph (5), the Minister of Education shall determine whether authorization should be granted and then notify the applicant of the results thereof by four months prior to the date on which such in-house college is planned to open. <Amended on Feb. 29, 2008; Mar. 23, 2013>
  (7) Any applicant who has been served with a notice on approval of his or her plan under paragraph (4) shall, where he or she is unable to file an application for authorizing the establishment of an in-house college within the period referred to in paragraph (5), file an application for the postponement of authorization for the establishment of such in-house college, accompanied by data attesting the grounds therefor, with the Minister of Education by the prescribed period. In such cases, the period that can be extended for filing an application for authorizing the establishment of an in-house college shall not exceed three years. <Amended on Feb. 29, 2008; Mar. 23, 2013>
  (8) Where the Minister of Education recognizes the existence of any inevitable reasons, he or she may adjust the period of paragraphs (1) and (4) through (6) within the scope of three months. <Amended on Feb. 29, 2008; Mar. 23, 2013>

Article 36-2 (Modification of authorization for establishment of in-house colleges) Where any person who has obtained authorization for the establishment of an in-house college pursuant to Article 32 (1) of the Act intends to modify the following matters pursuant to Article 38-2 (1) of the Act, he or she shall obtain authorization from the Minister of Education:
  1. Name;
  2. Objectives;
  3. A person who establishes such distance college-type educational establishment;
  4. Location;
  [This Article Added on Jun. 30, 2014]

Article 37 Deleted. <Oct. 20, 2008>

Article 38 (Scope of operating expenses of in-house colleges) Educational expenses borne by an employer under Article 32 (3) of the Act shall be the personnel expenses, the expenses incurred in relation to installation and maintenance of facilities and equipment, the expenses incurred in relation to experiments and teaching practices, the general management expenses and other incidental expenses. <Amended on Jun. 30, 2014>

Article 39 (Standards for establishment of in-house colleges) (1) Standards for establishment of in-house colleges under Article 32 (4) of the Act shall be as follows: <Amended on Jun. 30, 2014>
  1. School buildings shall be secured under Article 40;
  2. At least a half of the maximum number of teachers shall be secured under Article 41 and the remainder shall be secured within one year after such in-house college is opened.
  (2) Where any in-house college increases the maximum number of students, it shall make the entire number of students, including the increased maximum number of students, comply with standards prescribed in this Decree.
  (3) The classification of the maximum number of students by the course of study, which serves as the standards for computing the school buildings and the number of teachers under paragraph (1), shall be listed in Appendix 4.

Article 40 (School buildings of in-house colleges) (1) Each in-house college shall secure a school building according to the classification as listed in Appendix 5 in a place that is appropriate for educational and research activities. <Amended on Aug. 11, 2009>
  (2) The area of a school building to be secured under paragraph (1) shall be not less than 1/2 of the aggregated area that derives from the multiplication of the standard school building area per student as listed in Appendix 6 by the maximum number of students by the course of study based on the year in which the maximum numbers of teachers and students are set. In such cases, where the aggregated maximum number of students by the course of study falls short of 50 (this shall apply to a course of study for a technical bachelor's degree and that for a bachelor's degree, respectively, under Article 44 (1); hereinafter the same shall apply), the maximum number of students shall be deemed 50 and the method of computing in terms of the maximum number of students by the course of study shall be prescribed by Decree of the Ministry of Education. <Amended on Feb. 29, 2008; Mar. 23, 2013>
  (3) Where distance education facilities prescribed by Decree of the Ministry of Education are installed, the area of a school building under paragraph (2) may be reduced by up to 1/2. <Amended on Feb. 29, 2008; Mar. 23, 2013>

Article 41 (Teachers of in-house colleges) (1) Each in-house college shall secure the number of teachers that derives from the division of the maximum number of students by the course of study by the number of students per teacher as listed in Appendix 7 based on the year in which the maximum numbers of teachers and students are set. In such cases, where the maximum number of students by the course of study falls short of 50, the maximum number of students shall be deemed 50 and the method of computing in terms of the maximum number of students by the course of study shall be prescribed by Decree of the Ministry of Education. <Amended on Feb. 29, 2008; Mar. 23, 2013>
  (2) Teachers under paragraph (1) shall meet the qualification standards listed in the Appendix of the Regulations on the Standards for Qualifications of University Faculty Members and those who fall under any of the following may concurrently serve as teachers. In such cases, standards for selecting such persons who may concurrently serve as teachers (hereinafter referred to as "concurrent teachers") shall be prescribed by Decree of the Ministry of Education: <Amended on Feb. 29, 2008; Feb. 29, 2012; Mar. 23, 2013; Jun. 11, 2019>
  1. Teachers under Article 14 (1) and (2) of the Higher Education Act (excluding instructors);
